compiled_state.title: As an operator, I want aws-deploy-handler.sh to package and deploy a Lambda handler that validates events against the canonical schema, enforces server-side privacy, and writes objects to S3 at the documented key.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Create the Python 3.13 Lambda handler (`plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/lambda-handler/`) plus `aws-deploy-handler.sh` that packages and updates the Lambda code. The handler validates incoming JSON against the canonical schema (telemetry-event-schema.md), enforces server-side defense-in-depth privacy (replaces `cited_excerpt` with null when `client_id != "dso-self"` AND `emit_excerpts != true`), writes to `s3://<bucket>/${client_id}/${YYYY-MM-DD}/${event_id}.jsonl`, returns 202 Accepted on success, 400 Bad Request on malformed. Pre-flight ordering check (verifies Lambda and bucket exist before deploy).
**Why**: This is the server-side half of the universal endpoint. Without it the Function URL accepts requests but has no logic.
**Scope**:
- IN: Lambda handler code, packaging, deploy script, 202/400 responses, S3 key structure, server-side excerpt stripping, full privacy truth table.
- OUT: Emit utility (separate story). Schema document (separate story). Provisioning scripts (separate stories).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, POSTing a canonical event JSON to the deployed Lambda Function URL results in an S3 object at `s3://<bucket>/${client_id}/${YYYY-MM-DD}/${event_id}.jsonl` and a 202 Accepted response.
  ← Satisfies: sc-2  (sc-2: "Lambda Function URL accepts canonical event JSON POST and persists it at the documented S3 key")
- When this story is complete, POSTing a malformed event (schema-invalid) to the Function URL returns 400 Bad Request and writes no S3 object.
  ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, POSTing an event with `client_id != "dso-self"`, `emit_excerpts` unset or false, and a populated `cited_excerpt` results in an S3 object whose `cited_excerpt` is null (server-side defense-in-depth).
  ← Satisfies: sc-4  (sc-4: "privacy enforced at TWO layers: Lambda handler verifies server-side")
- When this story is complete, POSTing an event with `client_id = "dso-self"` and a populated `cited_excerpt` results in an S3 object whose `cited_excerpt` is preserved verbatim.
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, POSTing an event with `client_id != "dso-self"` and `emit_excerpts = true` results in an S3 object whose `cited_excerpt` is preserved verbatim (emit_excerpts=true override honored server-side).
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, `aws-deploy-handler.sh` fails clearly when the Lambda function or S3 bucket does not yet exist (pre-flight ordering check).
  ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Security] Server-side stripping is defense-in-depth — never trust adapter-side enforcement alone.
- [Schema contract] Handler validation logic must consume the canonical schema document (telemetry-event-schema.md) as a vendored JSON schema in the deployment package.
- [Observability] Log validation failures to CloudWatch with enough context to debug client misbehavior without leaking PII.
- [S3 key] Date partition uses UTC YYYY-MM-DD to match query-stats.sh expectations.
- [Testing] Integration tests need a local mock Lambda framework (e.g., `lambda-local`, SAM local, or direct Python invocation) since real Lambda deployment is not available in CI.
- [Data integrity] S3 PutObject is overwrite-only despite the .jsonl extension. A retried client emission with the same event_id will overwrite the prior object. Either use S3 conditional writes (`IfNoneMatch=*` to return 412 on collision) or document that overwrite-on-collision is an accepted tradeoff. Document the decision in the privacy/schema contract.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
